doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Sonny Greer passing for white and Bro the Creole in Birmingham
summary: Darensbourg relays Sonny Greer's story of a Birmingham restaurant where Bro of the Ellington band was refused service despite claiming to be Creole.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But it's funny, uh, uh, uh, you're the one that tell about, bro, about the Creole deal.

Uh, Sonny Greer was telling me this, uh, says, uh, they was playing in, uh, Birmingham, Alabama. And, uh, Sonny says, uh, Sonny says, actually, he says, nobody can tell that I'm, uh, colored, he says, uh. So, Sonny says, he went right downtown and started, and went in, uh, a white restaurant. Sonny Greer did? Yeah, Sonny Greer. When he, when, when, when Bro and them was with Duke, see? Okay. And Sonny says, uh, he was sitting in there, eating, and, uh, he says, Bro happened to pass by. And Bro seen him in there. So, Bro come in there and he says, uh, this counter where he was sitting, uh, he said, had an empty stool and Bro come sit down right next to him. Sonny says, uh, Sonny says, he kind of nudged Bro when he come in there. He says, look, man, he says, be careful. He says, don't talk to me. He says, you know, he says, I'm passing. He says, nobody can tell I'm colored. And he says, but you, he says, I don't know.
And Sonny, you know who could pass the best? Sonny had his hair all gassed and everything. Yeah. Sonny says, man, he says, I was all straight and everything.

He says, Bro sat on there. And he says, man, he says, I was eating a steak there. And he says, Bro sat on there for five minutes and for 10 minutes. And nobody waited on him. So finally Bro called the waitress over and says, uh, Miss, can I get a little service here? And the waitress looked at him and says, uh, says, I'm sorry. She says, but, uh, we don't serve colored people in here. He says, Bro looked at him.
What do you mean you don't serve colored people? He says, I, I will thank you to know that I'm a Creole. His waitress looked at him. He says, uh, I don't give a damn what you are and how old you are.
He says, we do not serve colored people. He says, oh, no. No. No. No. No. So, Joe, uh, what, what do you do after you, after O.C., uh, what's his name? What's his name? What's that, O.T.O.S.?
